# MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Machining radial ring rolling mill #1

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01

Scope
- This document defines lubrication and fluid handling for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01). It covers selection, application, verification, and recordkeeping for lubricants and auxiliary fluids used during machining operations in the P2-L3 line. Refer to MM-P2-L3-RR01 for comprehensive equipment maintenance tasks and to SOP-P2-L3-05 for safe work practices during fluid handling. Service bulletin SB-1036 contains vendor-supplied compatibility notes that must be reviewed prior to fluid changeovers.
- The maximum ring outer diameter for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is 1310 mm.

Background and rationale
- Proper lubricant selection and management preserve component life, ensure process stability, and reduce contamination risk to downstream operations. The lubricant specified for this machine balances film strength and wash-off resistance appropriate to the machining operations performed on the P2-L3 line. Using the correct lubricant reduces spindle and bearing wear, supports consistent surface finish, and mitigates corrosion risk during intermediate storage.
- Lubricant inventory and traceability are critical to satisfy manufacturing quality requirements and to support root cause analysis in the event of process excursions. The lubricant part number for Machining radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L3-RR01) is CFW-LUB-225. Only the specified lubricant shall be used unless written authorization is issued by maintenance engineering and documented with reference to SB-1036.

Tools and materials
- Approved lubricant: CFW-LUB-225. Use stock from labeled containers only. Reject containers with damaged seals or illegible labels.
- Personal protective equipment as defined in SOP-P2-L3-05.
- Clean transfer pump and dedicated dispensing nozzle marked for EQ-P2-L3-RR01 use.
- Clean, lint-free rags and capped waste bins for used materials.
- Secondary containment trays for fluid decanting operations.
- Portable collection vessels that are clean and dedicated to machining fluids to avoid cross-contamination.

Procedure
- Preparation
  - Review MM-P2-L3-RR01, SB-1036, and SOP-P2-L3-05 before starting. Confirm maintenance authorization and work order documentation is available.
  - Inspect CFW-LUB-225 containers for label integrity and expiry indicators. Verify the container seal is intact prior to opening.
  - Prepare secondary containment and position portable waste vessels. Don PPE per SOP-P2-L3-05.
- Drain and disposal
  - Isolate fluid circuits using approved lockout procedures. Capture used fluid in clean, labeled collection vessels. Prevent mixing of used fluids from different sources.
  - Transfer used fluid to waste storage in accordance with SB-1036 and plant environmental procedures. Record the batch or container identifier for traceability.
- Cleaning and inspection
  - Wipe accessible reservoirs and surfaces with lint-free rags to remove deposits. Inspect reservoirs and mating surfaces for signs of contamination, corrosion, or foreign material. Document findings on the work order and photograph any anomalies for inclusion in the maintenance record.
- Refill and fill verification
  - Use the dedicated transfer pump and nozzle to dispense CFW-LUB-225 into reservoirs. Avoid spills and overfilling by dispensing incrementally and checking fluid level visually as specified in MM-P2-L3-RR01.
  - After fill, run the machine through no-load cycles to circulate the fluid. Observe for leaks, foam, or unusual odors. If abnormal conditions appear, stop the machine and consult maintenance engineering and SB-1036 for corrective guidance.
- Post-maintenance actions
  - Reconcile used and new fluid quantities on the work order. Label replenished reservoirs with date and lubricant part number CFW-LUB-225.
  - Return tools and contaminated materials to designated bins. Complete all fields in the maintenance record, noting any deviations from procedure and corrective actions taken.
  - Notify process engineering if the work affected production parameters or if further sampling is recommended.

Examples and special cases
- Example: If a bulk transfer container has a compromised seal, do not use the material. Isolate the container, tag it with its container identifier, and notify stores and maintenance engineering for quarantine and testing per SB-1036.
- Example: If fluid exhibits visual degradation after circulation, collect a sample and initiate fluid analysis per plant sampling protocol. Retain the sample with the work order and reference MM-P2-L3-RR01 and SB-1036 for further disposition.

Acceptance criteria
- Fluid identification and quantity
  - Reservoirs and circulating systems must contain only CFW-LUB-225 where applicable. Work order and inventory records must show container identifiers and quantities used.
- Cleanliness and absence of contamination
  - Reservoirs and accessible wetted components shall be visibly free of sludge, metal flakes, or water pockets after cleaning steps. Any detected contamination shall be documented and addressed before returning equipment to service.
- Circulation and leak checks
  - After filling and circulation, no active leaks shall be present. If leakage persists, the machine remains out of service until repairs are completed and verified.
- Records and traceability
  - Completed maintenance work order must include:
    - Reference to this document id MM-P2-L3-RR01-S1.
    - Original lubricant container identifier and confirmation of CFW-LUB-225 usage.
    - Notes on any deviations and references to MM-P2-L3-RR01, SB-1036, and SOP-P2-L3-05 as applicable.
    - Photographs of reservoir condition where anomalies were found.
  - Maintain records in the document control system and attach to the equipment history per MM-P2-L3-RR01.

Records to keep
- Work order with signatures, container identifiers, and quantity reconciliation.
- Photographs and inspection notes for reservoirs and components.
- Any fluid analysis reports and quarantine records stemming from SB-1036 procedures.
- Copies of any authorizations for alternative lubricants or deviations, including reference to MM-P2-L3-RR01 and SOP-P2-L3-05.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-RR01
- SB-1036
- SOP-P2-L3-05
